# Minimum Description Length Unsupervisedly Separates Law-Grade from Statistical-Grade Knowledge in a Self-Improving Science Agent — and Reveals 86% of Its Own Discoveries Are Statistical

Wenbin Mao Affiliation: Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, Hooman
Biotechnology (Beijing) Co., Ltd.  
research.ai@xthinktank.com    Pei Zou Affiliation: Artificial
Intelligence Laboratory, Hooman Biotechnology (Beijing) Co., Ltd.  
research.ai@xthinktank.com

October 23, 2026

###### Abstract

AI systems that discover scientific relations now generate candidate
“laws” at scale, but the bottleneck has shifted from generation to
_vetting_: which candidates deserve belief? We show that a deployed
self-improving science agent—one that has admitted 252 relations through
held-out prediction courts—already computes the quantity that answers
this question: the Minimum Description Length compression ratio used for
model selection doubles, when read under discrete accounting, as an
unsupervised _epistemic grader_. The compression-ranked top band of the
agent’s ledger recovers exactly the canonical laws among its discoveries
(vis-viva across seven planets, Balmer/Rydberg) plus cross-measurement
identities— enrichment $`p=3.6\times 10^{-12}`$ under a hypergeometric
test—with zero counterexamples and physically coherent band structure.
The same lens retroactively reveals that 86% of the ledger compresses
nothing ($`\mathrm{cr}\approx 1`$): the agent had been recording
statistical regularities, including a learned predictor with held-out
$`R^{2}=0.541`$ admitted through the prediction gate, under a narrative
of compression as the unified value of knowledge—a narrative that was
never true for them. We formalize the resulting _dual-axis
bookkeeping_—prediction value ($`R^{2}`$) and compression value (cr) as
nearly decoupled axes of knowledge—demonstrate its robustness to
quantization, and register forward falsifiable predictions. The episode
is, to our knowledge, the first measured instance of a discovery agent
auditing its own knowledge ledger by an internal measure and finding
itself over-claiming.

## 1 Introduction

AI systems that discover scientific relations—symbolic regression
([Schmidt and Lipson, 2009](#bib.bib6)), concept-driven law discovery
([Fang et al., 2025](#bib.bib5)), and LLM-based pipelines—now generate
candidate “laws” at scale. The binding constraint has quietly shifted
from _generation_ to _vetting_: which of hundreds of admitted candidates
deserve belief? The concern is now institutional ([Cornelio et al.,
2026](#bib.bib10)), autonomous-research systems draw systematic critique
for exactly this gap ([Beel et al., 2025](#bib.bib11)), and the
symbolic-regression literature still grades discovery almost exclusively
by recovery of known ground-truth formulas ([Matsubara et al.,
2022](#bib.bib12))—a retreat made necessary by the absence of any grader
that works without ground truth. Human curation does not scale with the
output of a machine that never sleeps, and the systems themselves carry
no instrument that grades the epistemic status of what they find. A
discovery system that cannot tell a law from a strong correlation will
bank both under the same heading—and, given enough time, mistake its own
statistics for physics.

This paper reports that such an instrument already exists inside at
least one deployed system, because the quantity used for model selection
_is_ the grader when read correctly. The agent under study is a
self-improving physical-science runtime that has admitted 252 relations
through held-out prediction courts, each scored for predictive $`R^{2}`$
and for a Minimum Description Length (MDL) compression ratio ([Rissanen,
1978](#bib.bib1); [Grünwald, 2007](#bib.bib2)). Under the discrete
two-part accounting defined in
§[2](#S2 "2 System and Accounting ‣ Minimum Description Length Unsupervisedly Separates Law-Grade from Statistical-Grade Knowledge in a Self-Improving Science Agent — and Reveals 86% of Its Own Discoveries Are Statistical"),
the compression gain is effectively zero for statistical relations (the
ratio sits at parity, $`\mathrm{cr}\approx 1`$) and explodes only as
residuals approach determinism—a _law cliff_
(§[3](#S3 "3 The Law Cliff ‣ Minimum Description Length Unsupervisedly Separates Law-Grade from Statistical-Grade Knowledge in a Self-Improving Science Agent — and Reveals 86% of Its Own Discoveries Are Statistical")).
Auditing the ledger through this lens yields three findings:

1.  1.  Unsupervised law recovery
        (§[4](#S4 "4 Law Recovery: the Ledger Audit ‣ Minimum Description Length Unsupervisedly Separates Law-Grade from Statistical-Grade Knowledge in a Self-Improving Science Agent — and Reveals 86% of Its Own Discoveries Are Statistical")).
        The compression-ranked top band of the ledger consists exactly of
        the canonical laws and cross-measurement identities among the
        agent’s discoveries—the vis-viva relation across seven planets from
        JPL Horizons ephemeris, Balmer/Rydberg lines from NIST measurements,
        double-measurement and cell-volume identities—with enrichment
        $`p=3.6\times 10^{-12}`$ under a hypergeometric test and zero
        counterexamples.
2.  2.  A measured self-deception event
        (§[5](#S5 "5 The Self-Audit: 86% Statistical ‣ Minimum Description Length Unsupervisedly Separates Law-Grade from Statistical-Grade Knowledge in a Self-Improving Science Agent — and Reveals 86% of Its Own Discoveries Are Statistical")).
        The same lens shows 86% of the ledger (216 of 252 relations)
        compresses nothing ($`\mathrm{cr}\approx 1`$): the agent had been
        recording statistical regularities—including a learned predictor
        with held-out $`R^{2}=0.541`$ that passed the prediction gate—under
        a narrative of compression as the unified value of knowledge—a
        narrative that was never true for them. The narrative was written
        into the system’s written charter before the audit; the audit
        falsified it.
3.  3.  Dual-axis bookkeeping
        (§[5](#S5 "5 The Self-Audit: 86% Statistical ‣ Minimum Description Length Unsupervisedly Separates Law-Grade from Statistical-Grade Knowledge in a Self-Improving Science Agent — and Reveals 86% of Its Own Discoveries Are Statistical")).
        Prediction value and compression value are nearly decoupled axes:
        $`R^{2}=0.9`$ still yields $`\mathrm{cr}=1.06`$. A discovery agent
        that optimizes only prediction will accumulate statistics and
        mistake them for laws. We record the corrective—dual bookkeeping
        with explicit grades—and register forward falsifiable predictions
        (§[6](#S6 "6 Forward Falsifiable Preregistration ‣ Minimum Description Length Unsupervisedly Separates Law-Grade from Statistical-Grade Knowledge in a Self-Improving Science Agent — and Reveals 86% of Its Own Discoveries Are Statistical"))
        that make the grading claim testable rather than retrospective.

To our knowledge this is the first measured instance of a discovery
agent auditing its own knowledge ledger by an internal measure and
finding itself over-claiming. The math is not new—it is a Gaussian
shadow of Kolmogorov’s structure function ([Vereshchagin and Vitányi,
2004](#bib.bib3)), and we claim no theoretical contribution. What is new
is the demonstration that in a running system the measure separates laws
from statistics at $`10^{-12}`$ significance, that the failure mode it
exposes is real and was present, and that the fix is an accounting
convention rather than a new mechanism.

## 2 System and Accounting

### The agent.

The system is a self-improving physical-science runtime (companion paper
([Mao and Zou, 2026](#bib.bib8))). Concretely, it continuously ingests
public measurement archives (planetary ephemerides, spectroscopy tables,
crystallography databases, climate and geophysical records), proposes
parametric relations of the form $`y\approx f(x;\theta)`$ between
measured variables of one dataset, and admits a relation only if it
beats a standard basis on a held-out split—gates vary by court family,
typically $`R^{2}\geq 0.5`$ with a margin over the basis. Every admitted
relation (“symbol”) enters a persistent ledger.

### What “agent” means here.

We use the word in its classical sense ([Russell and Norvig,
2021](#bib.bib9)): an entity that perceives its environment (measurement
archives), acts autonomously on it (admitting, rejecting, registering
predictions), and maintains persistent state toward its goal (a ledger
of court-verified knowledge). It is a long-running discovery runtime,
not a trained model, and not an LLM-based agent in the contemporary
harness sense: no language model proposes, admits, or grades any
relation in the audited ledger—candidates are parametric forms from
symbolic generators, and admission is decided by held-out statistics. A
separate coding agent (Acknowledgments) develops the runtime itself
under human approval; that activity lies outside the audited loop and is
not claimed as the system’s own autonomy.

### Discrete two-part accounting.

For a target $`y`$ of variance $`\sigma_{y}^{2}`$ over $`n`$ samples, a
model’s residual $`\sigma_{r}^{2}`$, and quantization
$`\delta=\sigma_{y}\cdot 10^{-6}`$, the residual code is
$`\frac{n}{2}\log_{2}\!\left(2\pi e\,\sigma_{r}^{2}/\delta^{2}\right)`$
bits and the baseline code substitutes $`\sigma_{y}^{2}`$. The
description length of the fitted form is added to the model side. The
compression ratio is $`\mathrm{cr}=\text{baseline}/\text{total}`$. Two
properties matter here. First, $`\mathrm{cr}`$ is _not_ a monotone
re-labeling of $`R^{2}`$: it depends on
$`\log(\sigma_{r}^{2}/\delta^{2})`$, so variance reduction trades
against the quantization floor. Second, exact relations—residuals at the
floor—saturate the residual code while the baseline grows with
$`-\log\delta`$, so $`\mathrm{cr}\to\infty`$ as quantization refines:
determinism, not fit quality, buys compression.

### Provenance.

Every relation in the law band traces to external measurement: planetary
state vectors from JPL Horizons ephemerides (positions and velocities;
the vis-viva variables are $`r=|\mathbf{x}|`$ and
$`v^{2}=|\dot{\mathbf{x}}|^{2}`$), hydrogen line wavelengths from NIST
tables, crystallographic cell parameters from COD. No law-band relation
was generated from the formula it rediscovers; the audit is not
circular.

## 3 The Law Cliff

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

Figure 1: Compression ratio as a function of held-out predictive
$`R^{2}`$ under the agent’s discrete two-part accounting. The curve
rises logarithmically: even $`R^{2}=0.9`$ yields $`\mathrm{cr}=1.06`$;
compression explodes only as residuals approach the quantization floor,
i.e., deterministic law-hood. The two axes are nearly decoupled across
the statistical regime: a strong learned predictor (embedding)
compresses nothing.

Figure [1](#S3.F1 "Figure 1 ‣ 3 The Law Cliff ‣ Minimum Description Length Unsupervisedly Separates Law-Grade from Statistical-Grade Knowledge in a Self-Improving Science Agent — and Reveals 86% of Its Own Discoveries Are Statistical")
plots $`\mathrm{cr}(R^{2})`$ under the agent’s accounting. The curve is
nearly flat over the statistical regime: $`R^{2}=0.541`$ gives
$`\mathrm{cr}=1.004`$ (the agent’s best learned predictor sits exactly
on the curve); even $`R^{2}=0.9`$ gives only $`1.06`$; $`R^{2}=0.99`$
gives $`1.15`$. Compression explodes only in the last decimal places of
residual variance—$`R^{2}=1-10^{-12}`$ gives $`\mathrm{cr}=8.7`$—because
only there do residuals reach the quantization floor. The cliff sits at
_determinism_, not at “good prediction.”

The split is structural, not an artifact of the quantization scale.
Refining $`\delta`$ from $`\sigma_{y}\cdot 10^{-3}`$ to
$`\sigma_{y}\cdot 10^{-12}`$ widens the law/statistic separation ratio
monotonically ($`4.7\times\to 16.5\times`$): any exact relation
eventually dominates any statistical one, while statistical relations
converge to $`\mathrm{cr}\approx 1`$ from below or above depending on
description cost. No choice of $`\delta`$ reorders the two classes. By
construction $`\delta=\sigma_{y}\cdot 10^{-6}`$ makes the baseline
$`n\cdot 21.3`$ bits regardless of the variable’s scale: $`\mathrm{cr}`$
is scale-free, and sample size enters only through description
amortization.

We claim no novelty for the mathematics; it is a Gaussian-code instance
of the structure/statistics separation formalized by Kolmogorov’s
structure function and algorithmic statistics ([Vereshchagin and
Vitányi, 2004](#bib.bib3)), and the noise-floor intuition traces to
Shannon. The contribution is that a running discovery system can carry
this separation as a live ledger column—and that, read correctly, the
column already answers the vetting question.

Figure 2: All 252 relations admitted by the agent’s prediction gates,
ranked by compression ratio; red triangles mark canonical laws and
cross-measurement identities (labeling fixed before ranking). The top
band ($`\mathrm{cr}>1.5`$) is entirely law-grade (8/8, hypergeometric
$`p=3.6\times 10^{-12}`$); all seven vis-viva instances compress above

(1.24)—between deterministic laws and the statistical floor, exactly
where a law of that character belongs.

Figure [2](#S4.F2 "Figure 2 ‣ 4 Law Recovery: the Ledger Audit ‣ Minimum Description Length Unsupervisedly Separates Law-Grade from Statistical-Grade Knowledge in a Self-Improving Science Agent — and Reveals 86% of Its Own Discoveries Are Statistical")
ranks all 252 admitted relations by $`\mathrm{cr}`$. Red triangles mark
relations that are canonical laws or cross-measurement identities under
a labeling protocol fixed before ranking (13 labels among 252:
vis-viva$`\times`$7, Balmer/Rydberg$`\times`$2,
double-measurement$`\times`$2, cell-volume identities$`\times`$2
counting the conservation form, Gutenberg–Richter$`\times`$1).

The top band is the law band. All eight relations above
$`\mathrm{cr}>1.5`$ carry labels—vis-viva on Mercury, Mars, Venus,
Jupiter; the two Rydberg forms; the spectral double-measurement
identity; the cell-volume identity—against a null density of $`13/252`$.
The hypergeometric tail probability is $`3.6\times 10^{-12}`$. Below the
band the picture stays coherent: all seven vis-viva instances compress
above $`1.2`$ with Mercury ($`4.62`$) far above the rest; the
Gutenberg–Richter relation—a real but _statistical_ law—falls at
$`\mathrm{cr}=1.24`$, between the deterministic band and the statistical
floor, exactly where a law of that character belongs. We searched the
low-$`\mathrm{cr}`$ region for any admitted relation that a physicist
would call law-grade: there are none. The recovery is complete and clean
on this ledger.

### Robustness.

The threshold is not load-bearing: across $`\mathrm{cr}>1.2`$ to
$`>3.0`$ the top band remains fully labeled ($`12/15`$, $`10/12`$,
$`8/8`$, $`8/8`$, $`5/5`$, $`3/3`$; $`p=5.6\times 10^{-17}`$ down to
$`1.1\times 10^{-4}`$). And because the ledger contains repeated forms
across domains (252 entries collapse to 62 unique forms—one
damped-oscillation template alone spans 170), we recompute the test
after deduplicating to one entry per form family: 4 law labels among 62,
top band $`4/4`$, $`p=1.8\times 10^{-6}`$. Under the most conservative
independence assumption the separation survives by four orders of
magnitude.

Two caveats keep the claim honest. The enrichment is measured on one
ledger with a hand-fixed label protocol; we therefore register forward
predictions
(§[6](#S6 "6 Forward Falsifiable Preregistration ‣ Minimum Description Length Unsupervisedly Separates Law-Grade from Statistical-Grade Knowledge in a Self-Improving Science Agent — and Reveals 86% of Its Own Discoveries Are Statistical"))
rather than generalize retrospectively. And the ranking rewards
deterministic structure _relative to measurement precision_: a law
observed noisily would grade statistically until precision improves—the
grader measures the ledger, not nature directly.

## 5 The Self-Audit: 86% Statistical

The same
Figure [2](#S4.F2 "Figure 2 ‣ 4 Law Recovery: the Ledger Audit ‣ Minimum Description Length Unsupervisedly Separates Law-Grade from Statistical-Grade Knowledge in a Self-Improving Science Agent — and Reveals 86% of Its Own Discoveries Are Statistical")
carries the uncomfortable half of the result. 216 of 252 relations
($`86\%`$) have $`\mathrm{cr}\leq 1.0`$; the median is exactly
$`1.000`$. The agent’s written design charter had, for weeks, described
compression as the unified value of its knowledge. The audit shows the
account was unified in name only: for the overwhelming majority of the
ledger, nothing was being compressed. The narrative was falsified by its
own bookkeeping once the bookkeeping was read under the correct
(discrete) convention—an earlier differential-entropy reading had even
produced meaningless negative-bit ratios, which we document as a
caution.

The sharpest case is deliberate. In the week before the audit, a
context-embedding predictor for protein secondary-structure content was
trained on the agent’s sequence digest—by the development process under
human approval, per the agent-scope paragraph above, not by the runtime
autonomously—and admitted through the prediction gate as the first
“embedding symbol”: held-out $`R^{2}=0.541`$ against a symbolic ceiling
of $`0.277`$. Its compression ratio is $`1.004`$. Under single-metric
bookkeeping this admission would read as a law-grade discovery; under
the ledger it is what it is—the agent’s best predictor, statistical
grade, honestly labeled. The dual-axis correction is now a standing
system-level rule: $`R^{2}`$ records prediction value, cr records
compression value. Concretely, every admission carries the compression
ratio as a mandatory ledger field, while the admission-time $`R^{2}`$ is
preserved in the court artifact each entry’s evidence record links to.

This is the self-audit half of the paper’s claim, and we state it
plainly: a self-improving discovery system that cannot grade its own
knowledge will systematically mistake statistical accumulation for
physical understanding. Ours did, measurably, at $`86\%`$, until an
internal instrument—one it had been computing all along—said so.

## 6 Forward Falsifiable Preregistration

Retrospective enrichment alone could survive selection concerns. Two
predictions were registered at audit time and remain open:

1.  1.  _Statistical planes stay statistical._ All future admissions from
        the protein/chemical data planes (whose relations are corpus
        statistics, not exact functional identities) shall carry
        $`\mathrm{cr}\leq 1.5`$. A single protein-plane relation above
        $`1.5`$ without an identity/conservation construction falsifies the
        grading claim.
2.  2.  _New laws surface unaided._ The next genuinely exact relation
        admitted on any plane (e.g., a conserved quantity measured two ways)
        shall appear in the law band without human relabeling.

## 7 Related Work

### Algorithmic statistics.

Kolmogorov’s structure function and its modern treatment ([Vereshchagin
and Vitányi, 2004](#bib.bib3)) give the complete theory of separating
structure from noise in a datum. Our cr is a practical Gaussian-code
shadow of that separation, applied not to one string but to a live
ledger of fitted relations; we borrow the theory and demonstrate the
bookkeeping.

### Compression as drive.

Schmidhuber’s compression-progress principle ([Schmidhuber,
2008](#bib.bib4)) motivates discovery agents by compression gains. We
share the premise, not the direction: our question is not what
compression can drive, but what an already-computed compression column
_knows_ about knowledge already banked.

### Law discovery systems.

Symbolic regression ([Schmidt and Lipson, 2009](#bib.bib6)) and
concept-driven systems such as AI-Newton ([Fang et al.,
2025](#bib.bib5)) produce and organize candidate laws; AI-Newton
classifies laws by _scope of validity_ (specific vs. general), with no
compression accounting and no epistemic grading of output. To our
knowledge no discovery system grades its own ledger by description
length; searches for such precedent returned nothing direct.

### Philosophy of science.

The laws-vs-regularities debate ([Cartwright, 1983](#bib.bib7)) is the
background question. We do not enter it theoretically; we contribute an
operational instrument that a running system used on itself.

## 8 Limitations

Single system, single ledger ($`n{=}252`$), one labeling protocol; the
enrichment claim is an existence proof pending replication on other
ledgers. The grader measures relations-relative-to-precision, not
laws-in-nature. Literature coverage spanned Tavily, OpenAlex, and
Crossref; residual search risk remains. The vis-viva gradient across
planets is irregular beyond Mercury’s dominance, and we claim no clean
ordering.

## 9 Conclusion

A discovery agent’s model-selection arithmetic, read under discrete
two-part accounting, is an unsupervised epistemic grader: on a
252-relation operational ledger it recovered the law band at
$`p=3.6\times 10^{-12}`$, exposed an $`86\%`$ statistical majority
hiding under a unified-value narrative, and forced a standing dual-axis
correction. The grading claim remains falsifiable through the two
registered forward predictions, and the audit itself is replayable from
the archived ledger and scripts. Vetting infrastructure for
machine-generated science does not always need to be built; sometimes it
is already computed, waiting to be read honestly.

### Data availability.

The audited ledger, the audit scripts, and all figure-generating records
are archived in the project repository and available from the authors.
